convoLines.text: "Don't mind me. Today's just heavy. No time to waste."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Avery doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
James has an edge today — something curdled.
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing. That means something."
"We lost Tiana and Heidi. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"We never finished talking about grief — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'We're done for now. Not done-done. For now.'"
"Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"Have you heard what they're calling Drum-Belly? Gunther is pushing 'Loud-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"About grief — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"That's enough for now. It'll percolate."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'You're a good listener, you know that? A tired smile.' We still owe grief a proper ending, too."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I be honest? I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."

"It's my older sister, Nancy. Was taken. She raised me more than our mother did. Boring. That is what they wrote down. Some nights I dream about the pods -- rows of them, humming. I wake up and I can't tell if it was a dream or a broadcast."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Have you heard what they're calling Hummice? Gunther is pushing 'The Loud Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Avery doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We never did finish talking about grief — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing. That means something.'"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with James. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that. That's where we are."
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The whole fire was arguing about Hummice last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Loud Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"My part? I sleep in short shifts and pretend I'm not choosing sides."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
«Ciao! Tu... come ti chiami?» "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Proprio così, parola mia.» They nod back, slowly.
«Sei un tesoro, grazie di cuore.» (you catch 'tesoro' — treasure, 'cuore' — heart) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Sei una brava persona.» (you catch 'brava' — good) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Quanti giorni siamo qui? Tanti?» (you catch 'giorni' — days)
Davide laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — È vero.." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset. That's my read."
"This one — Peanut. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Being a community gardener taught me to read people fast — who's lying, who's scared, who needs a job. Turns out that's a survival skill. Who knew."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on your useful old-life skills. Do you understand?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be in charge. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Have you heard anything? About the taken. The pods. Anything at all."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Short version — Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
You show them Peanut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Actually, forget it."
"...Where was I? Gone. Ask me something else."

convoLines: "Don't mind me. Today's just heavy. No time to waste."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Avery doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
"Every laugh out there feels wrong today. Then I feel wrong for thinking it."
James has an edge today — something curdled.
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing. That means something."
"We lost Tiana and Heidi. I do the headcount without thinking. Then I think."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
